findings.reason: this is the exact hazard `c-hold-s5-scope` recorded as the reason §5 stays held, and the section was moved to `implementable` on the claim that it is gone, so a node built from it would run an irreversible `crew gc --apply` across every project's runs while its evidence fragment reported the pass as project-scoped.
findings.text: "The pass is scoped to the project it is invoked for" and the sentence that follows assert a scoping the code does not have: `_unledgered_run_directories` iterates `runs_root` with no project argument, spares a directory only when its run id is in some registered mount's ledger (`reckon/crew/routing.py:2177`), and removes it otherwise, so `gc --apply --project reckon` deletes another project's unledgered run directory; two further sweeps in the same call are unscoped as well (`_orphan_ledger_indexes` and `_stale_run_locks`, `reckon/crew/gc.py:1198-1231`)

findings.reason: a coordinator dispatching §5 would expect a dependency the plan's own sections do not provide, and the node can neither build nor verify the scoping it is judged on.
findings.text: the done-when now depends on a project-scoped unledgered sweep that no section delivers: the sweep is `reckon/crew/routing.py:2130`, and the call is `reckon/crew/gc.py:1214`, both outside §5's write paths and unowned by any other section

findings.reason: a criterion no output can satisfy leaves the section's gate unmeasurable, and the neighbouring "the drop equals the counts the report named" then compares against a report that omits exactly those directories.
findings.text: "An unledgered run directory whose pointer, manifest or name places it in another project is listed as kept, with that project named, and never removed" names a row the report never carries: the row is built with only `run_id`, `path`, `size`, `age_days`, `action` and `removed` (`reckon/crew/routing.py:2182-2189`), no project attribution exists in the sweep, and every directory it spares is skipped before a row is appended (`routing.py:2177`)

findings.reason: the fleet node serves every live orchestrator session on the machine, and the pass starves them, so the done-when should name a compute partition for it.
findings.text: "Every command runs on the fleet node with a timeout" places the pass on the coordination allocation, while a destructive sweep that walks the whole run store for sizes (`tree_size_bytes` per directory, 5,048 at measurement) belongs on a compute partition

findings.reason: the claim it supports is false anyway, so re-citing the anchor changes no outcome on its own.
findings.text: "`garbage_collect` reclaims only directories the project's ledger knows (`gc.py` near line 767)" cites a line inside the `sweep_exec_identities` docstring, unrelated to any run-directory reclaim

findings.reason: §5 is un-deferred on a four-day-old figure, and §7 retires 500 directories a pass, so §5's population may not exist by dispatch.
findings.text: "What remains is the population itself: 22,350 run directories" is stale: the store held 5,048 entries when measured on 2026-11-14, and the hourly retirement that `crew-state-stays-bounded` §7 runs across every project is what shrank it

rubric_items.anchors_resolve: a finding — `gc.py` near line 767 resolves, but to `sweep_exec_identities`, not to the run-directory reclaim the sentence describes, which lives at `reckon/crew/gc.py:1214` and `reckon/crew/routing.py:2130-2201`.
rubric_items.done_when: a finding — the new criterion "listed as kept, with that project named" names a row gc never emits, and "Every command runs on the fleet node" places an irreversible walk of the whole run store on the coordination node, against the standing fleet-node allocation rule.
rubric_items.evidence_paths: pass — the log lands in the run's own log directory and the before/after figures in `docs/evidence/fragments/the-crew-home-has-a-bound/the-existing-backlog-is-reclaimed.html`, neither on a node-local temporary path, and both survive the run.
rubric_items.naming: pass — the new text introduces no plan labels, ticket numbers or version tags, and names its records and counts by what they measure.
rubric_items.reasoning: a finding — the section states the pass is scoped to the project it is invoked for and that gc reclaims only ledger-known directories, both of which the code it describes contradicts.
rubric_items.single_goal: pass — §5 carries one operational deliverable, one reclaim of the run store, and its done-when closes on that one measure.
rubric_items.wiring: a finding — §5's done-when now requires a project-scoped unledgered run-directory sweep, and no section builds it: `_unledgered_run_directories` takes no project argument (`reckon/crew/routing.py:2130-2138`), the call site passes none (`reckon/crew/gc.py:1214-1221`), and §5's write paths are the run's log directory and one evidence fragment, so the code its done-when measures is outside this section and owned by no other.
